 Twice the fun
 Nxled battles Creamline for semis bonus
 Mark Escarlote · 17 November 2026 · 1:08 AM PHT · 3 MIN READ 
 BROOKE Van Sickle and the rest of undefeated Nxled go for a twice-to-beat semifinal bonus when they go up against Creamline on Tuesday in the PVL Season 10 All-Filipino Conference Siklab series at the Philsports Arena in Pasig.
 PHOTOGRAPH COURTESY OF PVL
 Text size A− Reset A+ Save Games today: 
 (Philsports Arena) 
 1 p.m. --- ZUS Coffee vs Akari 
 Also read LPU-B spikers seek maiden UCAL crown 
 3:30 p.m. --- NU vs 3B 
 6 p.m. --- Nxled vs Creamline 
 Undefeated Nxled aims to secure a semifinals twice-to-beat advantage in a marquee showdown against skidding defending champion Creamline in the Premier Volleyball League (PVL) Season 10 All-Filipino Conference Siklab Series today at the Philsports Arena in Pasig City.
 The Final Four-bound Chameleons will ride the crest of their six-game winning streak at the 6 p.m. main game and add to the Cool Smashers’ losing woes.
 Former Season Most Valuable Player Brooke Van Sickle, MJ Phillips, Jackie Acuna and Myla Pablo have been consistently playing at a high level as the four-year-old franchise remains steady in its bid for a breakthrough crown.
 Also read
 VOLLEY Who can stop Nxled?
 Red-hot Chameleons aim to stay perfect, seek semis spot
 Mark Escarlote · 12 November 2026 
 Holding a 6-0 win-loss record for the solo top spot, a top two finish for Nxled is already within reach.
 All the Italian Ettore Guidetti-coached squad needs to do is seize the opportunity in its last two elimination round assignments.
 Nxled is coming off back-to-back straight sets victories after dominating Capital1 and Akari.
 Even with momentum on its side, there’s no letting up for the Chameleons, especially against the league’s winningest club eager to halt a two-game slide.
 Guidetti expects decorated setter Gel Cayuna to maximize the team's offensive options and prevent Creamline from settling into its familiar rhythm.
 Just as important will be maintaining defensive discipline, particularly in containing the Cool Smashers' varied attack and limiting their opportunities to dictate the pace.
 The Chameleons have been a menace at the net, averaging 13.5 kill blocks a game, which can help contain Creamline’s aggressive attacking.
 “I really think that the only way to play at our best is to prepare for all the games the way we have done in the last four or five months, trying to win every single game. Aside from the injury we had today, we know that we have great potential,” Guidetti said.
 After the Cool Smashers, Nxled will close its elims campaign on Saturday against also-ran ZUS Coffee. 
 “We also know that we are going to play against two teams with incredible potential. So, we will try our best, from the scouting team to Brooke (Van Sickle) to EJ (Carino). I have full trust that everybody is going to do their best,” the Italian mentor said. 
 However, the Chameleons might sit out Jonah Sabete-Escamillan after hurting her knee in the third set of their 27-25, 25-22, 26-24, win over the Chargers last Thursday.
 Creamline is in a precarious spot at solo third with a 4-2 record. Lurking behind the squad are other playoffs contenders PLDT and Choco Mucho, both sporting 4-3 cards.
 The Cool Smashers are in a must-win situation in their last two assignments, including a clash with second-running Farm Fresh on Saturday.

 VOLLEY Heavy hitters
 Can PLDT stop Creamline’s rampage?
 DT · 5 November 2026 
 Creamline dropped a sorry 25-23, 13-25, 23-25, 25-22, 13-15, decision against sister team Flying Titans last Thursday, a week after a four-set loss to PLDT.
 Another defeat will complicate things for the Cool Smashers and might cost them a Final Four appearance.
 Meanwhile, Akari and ZUS Coffee meet at 1 p.m. in a battle of eliminated teams.
 The Chargers are in sixth place with a 3-4 record while the Thunderbelles are looking to improve their 1-5 slate.
 In the Spikers’ Turf Invitational Conference, NU-Archipelago Builders (5-2) tries to bounce back from a loss last game when it squares off against 3B (1-6) at 3:30 p.m.
